speaker: Unknown
en: Everyone thinks that we're just waiting for the phone to ring for the next Anthropic to call us to invest.
zh: 大家都以为我们只是在等电话响，等着下一个 Anthropic 给我们打电话投资。

speaker: Unknown
en: That's completely false.
zh: 那完全是错的。

speaker: Unknown
en: Everyone at Sequoia is a hunter.
zh: Sequoia 的每个人都是猎人。

speaker: Unknown
en: If you look at founders you like versus founders who make money as a two by two matrix, your job is to figure out in which part of the quadrant we make money.
zh: 如果你把你看好的创始人和能赚钱的创始人做一个二乘二矩阵，你的工作是弄清楚我们在矩阵的哪个部分能赚钱。

speaker: Unknown
en: The best investments in all the funds are always the companies where the sponsor had the highest conviction.
zh: 所有基金中最好的投资总是那些发起人有最高信念的公司。

speaker: Unknown
en: We are only as good as our next investment.
zh: 我们只和我们的下一个投资一样好。

speaker: Unknown
en: That's not an easy job.
zh: 这不是一份容易的工作。

speaker: Unknown
en: If you want an easy job, you go do something else.
zh: 如果你想要一份容易的工作，你去别的地方吧。

speaker: Unknown
en: Credits to Sean when he brought in the SpaceX investment.
zh: 归功于 Sean 当他带来了 SpaceX 的投资。

speaker: Unknown
en: We vote on companies.
zh: 我们对公司进行投票。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think someone voted a one.
zh: 我想有人投了一票。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think right now, if you're going to invest in a new Neolab, you're basically investing in the Quora, in the StumbleUpon when Facebook X came about.
zh: 我认为现在，如果你要投资一个新的 Neolab，你基本上就是在投资 Facebook X 时代的 Quora，投资 StumbleUpon。

speaker: Unknown
en: This is 20VC with me, Harry Stebbings.
zh: 这是 20VC，我是 Harry Stebbings。

speaker: Unknown
en: Now, I am so excited for the show today because I get to welcome one of my oldest friends to the show.
zh: 现在，我对今天的节目感到非常兴奋，因为我能欢迎我最老的朋友之一来到节目。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah, he's a partner at Sequoia, which just raised $10 billion in new capital to bet on the next generation of winners in the AI wave.
zh: 是的，他是 Sequoia 的合伙人，Sequoia 刚刚筹集了 100 亿美元新资金，用于押注 AI 浪潮中的下一代赢家。

speaker: Unknown
en: He's also an incredible human being.
zh: 他也是一个非常了不起的人。

speaker: Unknown
en: You'll hear more about why in the show, but this episode is incredible because it is a behind the scenes glimpse into what makes Sequoia so special, how they find great companies, how they win them, how they pick them.
zh: 你会在节目中听到更多关于原因，但这集非常棒，因为它是窥探 Sequoia 如此特别的幕后，他们如何寻找伟大的公司，如何赢得它们，如何挑选它们。

speaker: Unknown
en: It is a incredible view into what makes the great so good.
zh: 这是一个令人难以置信的视角，了解为什么伟大的公司如此优秀。

speaker: Unknown
en: This is Sequoia like you've never seen Sequoia before.
zh: 这是你从未见过的 Sequoia。

speaker: Unknown
en: And it was again, one of the most special interviews for me to be able to sit down with one of my oldest friends.
zh: 再次，这对我来说是一次最特别的采访之一，能和我最老的朋友之一坐下来交谈。

speaker: Unknown
en: But before we dive into the show today, founders face a different set of challenges at every stage of growth.
zh: 但在我们深入今天的节目之前，创始人在增长的每个阶段都面临不同的挑战。

speaker: Unknown
en: For Sid Shate, co-founder and CEO of dMatrix, JP Morgan delivered the guidance and expertise to help navigate what came next.
zh: 对于 dMatrix 的联合创始人兼 CEO Sid Shate，JP Morgan 提供了指导和专业知识来帮助应对接下来的情况。

speaker: Unknown
en: He credits JP Morgan's high-touch approach with supporting dMatrix as it grew and expanded internationally.
zh: 他归功于 JP Morgan 的高接触方法支持了 dMatrix 的成长和国际扩张。

speaker: Unknown
en: Whether you're in the early days or expanding into new markets, JPMorgan helps startups navigate complexity with real confidence, offering personalized guidance and deep sector expertise.
zh: 无论你是在早期还是进入新市场，JPMorgan 帮助初创企业以真正的信心应对复杂性，提供个性化指导和深入的领域专业知识。

speaker: Unknown
en: Find out how JPMorgan helps founders at jpmorgan.com forward slash grow without limits.
zh: 了解 JPMorgan 如何帮助创始人，请访问 jpmoran.com forward slash grow without limits。

speaker: Unknown
en: JPMorgan is the bank of the innovation economy.
zh: JPMorgan 是创新经济的银行。

speaker: Unknown
en: While JP Morgan supports growth, Corgi protects it.
zh: 当 JP Morgan 支持增长时，Corgi 保护它。

speaker: Unknown
en: My word, what an arresting first line.
zh: 天哪，多么惊人的开场白。

speaker: Unknown
en: Get your ass covered with Corgi Insurance, and I'll tell you why.
zh: 用 Corgi Insurance 保护你的屁股，我会告诉你原因。

speaker: Unknown
en: If you're running a business right now, you already know this pain all too well.
zh: 如果你现在经营一家企业，你已经很了解这种痛苦了。

speaker: Unknown
en: Getting insurance, it's really slow, it's confusing, and my word, it's full of paperwork.
zh: 购买保险真的真的很慢，很困惑，天哪，全是文书工作。

speaker: Unknown
en: Well, that's exactly why Corgi is here to change the game.
zh: 这正是为什么 Corgi 来改变游戏规则。

speaker: Unknown
en: Corgi is the first and only insurance carrier designed specifically for tech companies
zh: Corgi 是第一家也是唯一一家专门为科技公司设计的保险承保商

speaker: Unknown
en: Allowing you to get covered in minutes instead of days, Corgi provides essential coverages for all growth stages such as D&O, E&O liability, cyber, commercial, general liability, and more.
zh: 允许你在几分钟内而不是几天内获得保障，Corgi 为所有成长阶段提供基本保障，如 D&O、E&O 责任险、网络险、商业一般责任险等。

speaker: Unknown
en: Get your ass covered, I love the way we say ass, with Corgi Insurance alongside thousands of other startups at Corgi.
zh: 用 Corgi Insurance 保护你的屁股，我喜欢我们说 ass 的方式，以及数千家其他初创企业，就在 Corgi。

speaker: Unknown
en: Visit corgi.com forward slash 20VC today.
zh: 今天访问 corgi.com forward slash 20VC。

speaker: Unknown
en: That's corgi.com forward slash 20VC.
zh: 那是 corgi.com forward slash 20VC。

speaker: Unknown
en: You won't regret it.
zh: 你不会后悔的。

speaker: Unknown
en: While Corgi covers risk, Flex gives you room to move.
zh: 当 Corgi 覆盖风险时，Flex 给你移动的空间。

speaker: Unknown
en: Business owners run their whole financial life on Flex.
zh: 企业主在 Flex 上运营他们的整个财务生活。

speaker: Unknown
en: One platform from business revenue to their personal spend.
zh: 一个平台，从企业收入到他们的个人消费。

speaker: Unknown
en: Float every purchase for 60 days.
zh: 每笔采购浮动 60 天。

speaker: Unknown
en: Tap capital that grows with your revenue and pay vendors in 170 countries across 32 currencies.
zh: 利用随你的收入增长的资本，并在 32 个货币的 170 个国家向供应商付款。

speaker: Unknown
en: Plus the whole back office, bills, expenses, accounting, all in one place.
zh: 加上整个后台，账单、费用、会计，都在一个地方。

speaker: Unknown
en: So you spend less time reconciling and more time growing.
zh: 所以你花更少的时间对账，花更多的时间成长。

speaker: Unknown
en: That's why thousands of owners use Flex, named one of Fast Company's most innovative companies of 2026.
zh: 这就是为什么成千上万的所有者使用 Flex，Flex 被 Fast Company 评为 2026 年最具创新力的公司之一。

speaker: Unknown
en: Visit flex.one, that's F-L-E-X dot O-N-E, and use the code 20VC.
zh: 访问 flex.one，也就是 F-L-E-X dot O-N-E，并使用代码 20VC。

speaker: Unknown
en: You have now arrived at your destination.
zh: 你现在已经到达了你的目的地。

speaker: Unknown
en: Dude, we have known each other, I was trying to think, I think it's been like eight, 10 years.
zh: 兄弟，我们认识彼此了，我在想，大概有八、十年了吧。

speaker: Unknown
en: Almost 10 years, yeah.
zh: 差不多 10 年了，是的。

speaker: Unknown
en: You were young back then, and now we're getting like- I remember- Aging.
zh: 你那时候很年轻，而现在我们变得像——我记得——变老了。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah, you were at Excel, and you were over there, very nice officers, and I was at, just joined Atomico, I think.
zh: 是的，你在 Excel，你在那边，非常好的官员们，而我在，我刚加入 Atomico，我想。

speaker: Unknown
en: And we were both like very young and we were like, wow, it worked.
zh: 我们两个那时都很年轻，我们就像，哇，它成功了。

speaker: Unknown
en: But I want to start because I think a lot of people will hear you now and think, wow, Sequoia partner and wow.
zh: 但我想从这里开始，因为我想很多人现在听到你会想，哇，红杉合伙人，以及哇。

speaker: Unknown
en: But there's something in particular about the relationship that you have with your parents and how you look after your father, which I think is an embodiment of what a great human you are.
zh: 但关于你和父母的关系以及你照顾你父亲的方式有一些特别之处，我认为这体现了你是一个多么棒的人。

speaker: Unknown
en: So can you just tell me a little bit about that before we dive into all the intellectual nerdy shit?
zh: 所以在我们深入所有知识分子书呆子狗屁之前，你能先告诉我一点关于那个的事情吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: Because I want people to know you a little bit first.
zh: 因为我想让大家先稍微了解你一点。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah, look, my dad suffers from a condition, biological condition, that showed up in my early 20s.
zh: 是的，听着，我父亲患有某种状况，生理状况，它出现在我 20 多岁刚出头时。

speaker: Unknown
en: I have no siblings, so when that happened, I started looking after him.
zh: 我没有兄弟姐妹，所以当那件事发生时，我开始照顾他。

speaker: Unknown
en: He's very unusual, my dad.
zh: 他非常不寻常，我父亲。

speaker: Unknown
en: He comes from a family of four.
zh: 他来自一个四口之家。

speaker: Unknown
en: I grew up in rural France, stopped school when he was 13.
zh: 我在法国农村长大，他在 13 岁时停止了上学。

speaker: Unknown
en: You know, he did that to put money on the table for the rest of his family.
zh: 你知道，他这样做是为了赚钱养家里的其他人。

speaker: Unknown
en: I saw him care for his parents when they were aging, and I just looked up to that.
zh: 当他父母年老时，我看到他照顾他们，我只是很崇拜那样。

speaker: Unknown
en: He's quite unusual.
zh: 他相当不寻常。

speaker: Unknown
en: He's an astrologer.
zh: 他是一名占星家。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah, not an astronomer, astrologer.
zh: 是的，不是天文学家，是占星家。

speaker: Unknown
en: So I always saw him kind of take a different path than when his disease started showing up.
zh: 所以我总是看到他走一条不同的道路，直到他的疾病开始显现。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah, I was there for him.
zh: 是的，我陪在他身边。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I know you've done the same for your parents, so...
zh: 而我知道你也对你的父母做了同样的事，所以……

speaker: Unknown
en: Do you know, I specialize in binary statements that get me either loved or hated.
zh: 你知道，我擅长于发表那些会让我要么被爱要么被恨的二元对立陈述。

speaker: Unknown
en: But I think one of the biggest pieces of bullshit advice is you've got to do it for you.
zh: 但我认为最大的废话建议之一就是你必须为你自己做。

speaker: Unknown
en: Everyone who says that I think is just talking out their ass.
zh: 每个说那话的人我认为都是在胡说八道。

speaker: Unknown
en: I do most of the things for my mother.
zh: 我做大多数事情都是为了我母亲。

speaker: Unknown
en: Did you know I adore my mom?
zh: 你知道我崇拜我妈妈吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: And I actually think you can achieve great things when you do it for someone else.
zh: 而且我真的认为当你为别人做时，你能取得伟大的成就。

speaker: Unknown
en: And that should be hailed and lauded, not do it for yourself always.
zh: 这应该被赞扬和称颂，而不是总是为你自己做。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah, my opinion is that if you have very clear values, everything else is easy.
zh: 是的，我的观点是，如果你有非常清晰的价值观，其他一切都很容易。

speaker: Unknown
en: It might be painful in the moment to stick to them, but it's just at least you have mental clarity about what you're doing, and it doesn't matter how much work you put in.
zh: 在当下坚持它们可能会很痛苦，但至少你对自己正在做的事情有心理上的清晰，而且你投入多少工作并不重要。

speaker: Unknown
en: You just know you're doing it for the right reasons.
zh: 你只是知道你做这件事是为了正确的理由。

speaker: Unknown
en: Absolutely, and the core value that we have is liquidity.
zh: 当然，我们的核心价值观是流动性。

speaker: Unknown
en: I don't think that's true in venture capital.
zh: 我不认为这在风险投资中是真的。

speaker: Unknown
en: Did you see, I tweeted the other day when Pat and Alfred were on TV, and they said, they were asked about Sean McGuire's tweets, and I said, Alfred's comment was the best I've seen, which is, well, we look at the balance sheet of Sean, and I just thought, when summarizing someone, we look at the balance sheet of X is like the greatest way to discuss that person.
zh: 你看到吗，我前几天发了一条推文，当 Pat 和 Alfred 上电视时，他们被问及 Sean McGuire 的推文，我说，Alfred 的评论是我见过的最好的，也就是，嗯，我们看 Sean 的资产负债表，我只是觉得，当总结某人时，我们看 X 的资产负债表是讨论那个人的最好方式。

speaker: Unknown
en: I got in a lot of trouble for that.
zh: 我因此惹了很多麻烦。

speaker: Unknown
en: You did?
zh: 你是吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah, yeah.
zh: 是的，是的。

speaker: Unknown
en: Oh my gosh.
zh: 天哪。

speaker: Unknown
en: Anyway, I want to dive into Sequoia a little bit.
zh: 总之，我想稍微深入聊聊红杉。

speaker: Unknown
en: You joined from Excel.
zh: 你是从 Excel 加入的。

speaker: Unknown
en: I want to know, what did you not know about Sequoia before joining that you now know having been there for several years now?
zh: 我想问，在你加入之前有哪些关于红杉的事情是你不知道，而现在已经知道并在那里待了好几年的？

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah, I've been there three years, but I've been doing venture capital for 10.
zh: 是的，我在那里待了三年，但我做风险投资已经 10 年了。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think Sequoia operates really like a sports team.
zh: 我认为红杉的运作真的像一支运动队。

speaker: Unknown
en: Maybe you've heard that story before, but this is my first day ever at Sequoia.
zh: 也许你以前听过那个故事，但这是我在红杉的第一天。

speaker: Unknown
en: I'm in California.
zh: 我在加州。

speaker: Unknown
en: I visited the office before, but I wake up early, jet lagged, and I show up to the office at maybe 4.30, 5 a.m. Something ridiculous like that.
zh: 我以前去过那个办公室，但我醒得很早，有时差，我在大概凌晨 4 点 30 分，5 点左右到了办公室。像这样荒谬的时间。

speaker: Unknown
en: I felt obviously very happy about myself.
zh: 我对自己显然感觉非常好。

speaker: Unknown
en: I was sent to the office that day.
zh: 那天我被派到了办公室。

speaker: Unknown
en: And as I approached the building, I see some light inside.
zh: 当我走近大楼时，我看到里面有一些光。

speaker: Unknown
en: And as I'm about to push the door, I see a man on the other side.
zh: 当我要推门时，我看到另一边有一个男人。

speaker: Unknown
en: And he looks at me.
zh: 他看着我。

speaker: Unknown
en: And with a deep voice, he goes, what are you doing here so early?
zh: 他用低沉的声音说，你这么早在这里做什么？

speaker: Unknown
en: And I'm a little surprised, but with pride, I tell him, I'm here to take my first call.
zh: 我有点惊讶，但带着自豪感，我告诉他，我是来这里接我的第一个电话的。

speaker: Unknown
en: What are you doing here so early?
zh: 你这么早在这里做什么？

speaker: Unknown
en: And he's like, I've already taken my first call, haha.
zh: 他就像，我已经接了我的第一个电话，哈哈。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then he just walked off, and he was just so happy about it.
zh: 然后他就走开了，而且他对这件事非常高兴。

speaker: Unknown
en: Still, you know, lost the game.
zh: 尽管如此，你知道，输了游戏。

speaker: Unknown
en: And that was Doug?
zh: 那个是 Doug 吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: That was Doug.
zh: 那是 Doug。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah, of course it was.
zh: 是啊，当然是他。

speaker: Unknown
en: Oh, Doug.
zh: 噢，Doug。

speaker: Unknown
en: Is that just like the Americans being built differently?
zh: 这是不是就像美国人的体质构造不同？

speaker: Unknown
en: Do you see everyone else at Sequoia do that and feel you have to do the same?
zh: 你看到 Sequoia 的其他人都这样做，觉得你也必须这样做吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: Is that it?
zh: 是那样吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: I don't think so.
zh: 我不这么认为。

speaker: Unknown
en: We just hire people who are built like that.
zh: 我们只是雇佣了那样构造的人。

speaker: Unknown
en: Doug is Italian.
zh: Doug 是意大利人。

speaker: Unknown
en: He's European by roots and immigrated to the US when he was very young.
zh: 他根源于欧洲，很小的时候移民到了美国。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I've only known him for a couple of years, but I'm pretty sure he was always like that.
zh: 我只认识他几年，但我很确定他一直就是那样。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I want to play dodgeball with him.
zh: 我想和他玩躲避球。

speaker: Unknown
en: What does everyone think they know about Sequoia that they actually get wrong?
zh: 大家以为他们知道关于 Sequoia 的哪些事，但实际上他们弄错了？

speaker: Unknown
en: Everyone thinks that we're just waiting for the phone to ring for the next Anthropic to call us to invest.
zh: 大家以为我们只是在等电话响，等着下一个 Anthropic 给我们打电话让我们投资。

speaker: Unknown
en: That's completely false.
zh: 那完全是错的。

speaker: Unknown
en: Everyone at Sequoia is a hunter.
zh: Sequoia 的每个人都是猎人。

speaker: Unknown
en: We were 11 people a couple of months back in the early team.
zh: 几个月前我们在早期团队里有 11 个人。

speaker: Unknown
en: That's basically what a football team is.
zh: 那基本上就是一个足球队。

speaker: Unknown
en: And everyone's just scoring on the field.
zh: 每个人都在场上得分。

speaker: Unknown
en: It doesn't matter how long you've been there.
zh: 你在那里待了多久并不重要。

speaker: Unknown
en: Everyone expects you to perform.
zh: 每个人都期待你表现。

speaker: Unknown
en: In fact, the younger you are, the more people expect experienced people to perform because you just need them more.
zh: 事实上，你越年轻，人们越期待经验丰富的人表现，因为你们更需要他们。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's very competitive out there.
zh: 外面的竞争非常激烈。

speaker: Unknown
en: And we think that people need to behave exceptionally well as individuals, but win as a team.
zh: 我们认为人们需要作为个人表现得特别好，但作为团队获胜。

speaker: Unknown
en: That's really important.
zh: 这真的很重要。

speaker: Unknown
en: I don't think that people understand that as much.
zh: 我不认为人们对此有足够的理解。

speaker: Unknown
en: I'll give you a story to illustrate it.
zh: 我给你讲个故事来说明它。

speaker: Unknown
en: Constantine Buehler, my partner, helped us lead the investment in Citadel Securities, Ken Griffin's company.
zh: Constantine Buehler，我的合伙人，帮助我们领投了对 Citadel Securities 的投资，Ken Griffin 的公司。

speaker: Unknown
en: They had never taken outside capital.
zh: 他们从未接受过外部资本。

speaker: Unknown
en: The reason we were able to invest is Constantine built a relationship with Ken since he was a student.
zh: 我们之所以能够投资，是因为 Constantine 从 Ken 还是学生的时候起就与他建立了关系。

speaker: Unknown
en: He had been his mentor for years and years.
zh: 他多年来一直是他的导师。

speaker: Unknown
en: And Constantine never gave up and just kept asking, can we invest?
zh: Constantine 从未放弃，一直在问，我们可以投资吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: Can we invest?
zh: 我们可以投资吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: Until Ken kindly said yes.
zh: 直到 Ken 好心地说了可以。

speaker: Unknown
en: Can I ask you, in that case, what does that deal look like?
zh: 那我可以问你，那种情况下，那笔交易是什么样的？

speaker: Unknown
en: I mean this not superciliously or glibly, but does Constantine come to IC on Monday and be like, I have a new startup for us.
zh: 我这么说并不是自以为是或轻率，Constantine 是在周一的 IC 会议上说，我有一家新公司给我们。

speaker: Unknown

en: I want to go back a step though, because that's like assuming that a sponsor likes a deal enough to take it there.

zh: 如果你回到解构是什么造就了伟大的创始人和像创始人阅读，你之前说过阅读创始人已经，公平地说，你的合伙人说过这一点，阅读创始人已经迅速成为了一种超能力。

zh: 你认为你做了什么让你擅长阅读创始人？

zh: 而我的做法是首先敞开心扉。

zh: 我告诉他们,成长过程中父母离异是怎样的,我的母亲是成功的女商人,在日内瓦湖上有着不错的景观。

speaker: Unknown

zh: 这很糟糕，但同时，它也向你展示了那个人走了多远的距离才到达今天的位置。

speaker: Unknown
en: And it doesn't mean that they'll continue on that path, but at least it tells you a lot about their existing trajectory.
zh: 这并不意味着他们会继续走那条路，但至少它告诉你很多关于他们现有轨迹的信息。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so your job is just to figure out if they're going to continue on that path or not.
zh: 所以你的工作只是弄清楚他们是否会继续走那条路。

speaker: Unknown
en: I totally agree with you.
zh: 我完全同意你。

speaker: Unknown
en: Distance traveled.

zh: 而且，就像，他们为了到达今天的位置所经历的狗屎事件实际上就是更多。

speaker: Unknown
en: I totally agree with you.
zh: 我完全同意你。

en: People answer that honestly, honestly.
zh: 人们诚实地回答这个问题，诚实。

en: What's interesting is how they answer the question.
zh: 有趣的是他们如何回答这个问题。

en: I've had founders be very direct about who their worst references were.
zh: 我曾有创始人非常直接地说出他们最差的推荐人是谁。

zh: 令人惊奇的是，然后我给那些人打电话，你会得到很多细节。

en: I'm not looking for perfection.
zh: 我不是在寻找完美。

en: Like, do you not find that?

en: Where like the best people just have, I don't know, I can't get it.

en: Are they going to go through the pain to keep doing what they're doing?

en: It's never enough.
zh: 永远是不够的。

en: It might not make them an outlier founder.

speaker: Unknown
en: Do you update your Netflix every time?
zh: 你每次都更新你的 Netflix 吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: I think they probably keep the emails just in case because some of them come back.
zh: 我想他们可能会保留邮箱以防万一，因为有些人会回来。

speaker: Unknown
en: Might come back.
zh: 可能会回来。

speaker: Unknown
en: Can you keep Karen at OpenAI just in case?
zh: 你能把 OpenAI 的 Karen 留着以防万一吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: What the fuck?
zh: 搞什么鬼？

speaker: Unknown
en: Is traditional private equity fucked?
zh: 传统的私募股权完了吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: I actually think they might do very well by investing in those companies that have the data and so on and won't be able to hire frontier talent, but they'll build very fine businesses.
zh: 我其实觉得他们可能做得很好，通过投资那些拥有数据等数据的公司，这些公司将无法雇佣顶尖人才，但会建立非常好的业务。

speaker: Unknown
en: They just also, they're not seeking the same outcomes that we seek.
zh: 只是还有，他们寻求的结果与我们寻求的不一样。

speaker: Unknown
en: We want to back the next trillion dollar company.
zh: 我们想支持下一个万亿级公司。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think it's unlikely that's a private equity backed company.
zh: 我认为这不太可能是一家私募股权支持的公司。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's true.
zh: 没错。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think the only thing that will vary is just, like, do they have the ability to do more deals?
zh: 我认为唯一会改变的只是，比如，他们有能力做更多交易吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: Because so many of them are underwater with shit deals.
zh: 因为他们中很多人在糟糕的交易中都被套牢了。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah, yeah.
zh: 是的，是的。

speaker: Unknown
en: When you're dealing with five Titanics, are you really willing to, like, let another flower blossom?
zh: 当你要处理五艘泰坦尼克号时，你还真的愿意让另一朵花绽放吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah.
zh: 是的。

speaker: Unknown
en: Tough.
zh: 很难。

speaker: Unknown
en: Listen, dude, I want to do a quick fire with you.
zh: 听着，伙计，我想和你来个快问快答。

speaker: Unknown
en: So I say a short statement, you give me your immediate thoughts.
zh: 所以我说一个简短的陈述，你给我你的即时想法。

speaker: Unknown
en: Sure.
zh: 没问题。

speaker: Unknown
en: What's the most overfunded category?
zh: 哪个类别资金过剩最严重？

speaker: Unknown
en: Probably legal.
zh: 可能是法律。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think there's just so many me too's in this category, whereas I think that the winner is already in existence.
zh: 我认为这个类别里有很多跟随者，而我认为赢家已经存在了。

speaker: Unknown
en: I'm obviously biased, but I think Harvey is very well positioned because they have the widest distribution.
zh: 我显然有偏见，但我认为 Harvey 处于非常有利的地位，因为他们拥有最广泛的分发。

speaker: Unknown
en: And yeah, I just don't understand investors' willingness to invest in the nth competitor.
zh: 是的，我只是不明白投资者投资第 n 个竞争对手的意愿。

speaker: Unknown
en: I will naturally say I think Agora is obviously going to win.
zh: 我自然会说我认为 Agora 显然会赢。

speaker: Unknown
en: But I think going back to your point, I think slope is what's important.
zh: 但我认为回到你的观点，我认为斜率才是重要的。

speaker: Unknown
en: I do agree with your overfundedness, but I kind of don't in a way actually do because I think legal is a very horizontal, broad market.
zh: 我确实同意你说的资金过剩，但我某种程度上不同意，实际上同意，因为我认为法律是一个非常横向的广泛市场。

speaker: Unknown
en: We're in a business called Solve Intelligence.
zh: 我们从事的业务叫做 Solve Intelligence。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's IP law, very specific for patent lawyers.
zh: 它是知识产权法，非常针对专利律师。

speaker: Unknown
en: That is so different to a lot of what Harvey and Agora do to the extent that both Harvey and Agora founders are invested in it.
zh: 这与 Harvey 和 Agora 做的很多事情非常不同，以至于 Harvey 和 Agora 的创始人都投资了它。

speaker: Unknown
en: Do you see what I'm saying?
zh: 你明白我的意思吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah, yeah.
zh: 是的，是的。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so I really think it's actually, you will see the unbundling of law.
zh: 所以我真的认为实际上，你将看到法律的解绑。

speaker: Unknown
en: Now, will Solve be as big as Harvey or Lacora?
zh: 现在，Solve 会像 Harvey 或 Lacora 一样大吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: No, but still multi-billion.
zh: 不，但仍然是数十亿级。

speaker: Unknown
en: Really interesting.
zh: 真的很有趣。

speaker: Unknown
en: Underfunded category that should be funded more?
zh: 哪个类别资金不足，应该获得更多资金？

speaker: Unknown
en: They call it BCI, Brain Computer Interfaces.
zh: 他们称之为 BCI，脑机接口。

speaker: Unknown
en: That's where all the smart kids are going.
zh: 那是所有聪明孩子都去的地方。

speaker: Unknown
en: So I'm a big believer that you should just follow where the smartest people are going.
zh: 所以我是一个坚定的信徒，你应该只追随最聪明的人去的地方。

speaker: Unknown
en: 10 years ago, the smartest people were going to ML and AI.
zh: 10 年前，最聪明的人都在去 ML 和 AI。

speaker: Unknown
en: 10 years from now, we'll see those companies probably blossom.
zh: 10年后，我们会看到那些公司大概会蓬勃发展。

speaker: Unknown
en: That's the next frontier.
zh: 那就是下一个前沿。

speaker: Unknown
en: The best agent company outside of Sequoia.
zh: 红杉之外最好的智能体公司。

speaker: Unknown
en: So the best agent company outside Sequoia is probably Cursor.
zh: 所以红杉之外最好的智能体公司大概是 Cursor。

speaker: Unknown
en: One, they're in one of the most important markets.
zh: 第一，他们处于最重要的市场之一。

speaker: Unknown
en: But second, where there was a lot of chatter around AI wrappers, they were the first company to really understand that you could post-train models and actually go deeper into the stack.
zh: 但第二，当有很多关于 AI 包装器的讨论时，他们是第一家真正理解你可以后训练模型并且真正深入到堆栈底层的公司。

speaker: Unknown
en: When that $60 billion deal happens, do you guys sit around the table and go, oh.
zh: 当那笔 600 亿美元的交易发生时，你们会围坐在桌旁说，噢。

speaker: Unknown
en: Well, they joined a portfolio company, so that helped.
zh: 嗯，他们加入了一家组合公司，所以这有帮助。

speaker: Unknown
en: Best angel who doesn't get enough credit?
zh: 哪位天使投资人最没有得到足够的认可？

speaker: Unknown
en: Gloria from Puzzle, I think deserves a lot of credit.
zh: Puzzle 的 Gloria，我认为 deserves 值得很多赞誉。

speaker: Unknown
en: She's got an incredible nose and works extremely hard for her founders.
zh: 她有着 incredible 不可思议的嗅觉，并且为她的创始人极其努力地工作。

speaker: Unknown
en: What myths haunts you most?
zh: 什么神话最困扰你？

speaker: Unknown
en: I think probably Trade Republic.
zh: 我大概是 Trade Republic。

speaker: Unknown
en: So we're in business with Trade Republic, but I looked at the seed before I joined Sequoia.
zh: 所以我们与 Trade Republic 有业务往来，但在我加入红杉之前我看过那个种子轮。

speaker: Unknown
en: I remember telling the founder question, I don't think you're going to succeed because Revolut is going to smoke you.
zh: 我记得告诉创始人一个问题，我认为你不会成功，因为 Revolut 会把你干掉。

speaker: Unknown
en: The point is, like, it turns out that they barely compete and they're both building amazing businesses.
zh: 关键是，结果发现他们几乎不竞争，而且他们都在建立 amazing 了不起的业务。

speaker: Unknown
en: I fail to understand.
zh: 我没能理解。

speaker: Unknown
en: It was not a winner-takes-all market.
zh: 那不是一个赢家通吃的市场。

speaker: Unknown
en: I underestimate the size of the category.
zh: 我低估了这个类别的规模。

speaker: Unknown
en: You know, one of the most BS reasons to miss a great company is, oh, well, people will use you at the start, but then when they become bigger, they'll just build their own.
zh: 你知道，错过一家伟大公司的一个最 BS（扯淡）的理由是，噢，好吧，人们一开始会使用你，但当他们变大时，他们就会自己构建。

speaker: Unknown
en: The classic Stripe.
zh: 经典的 Stripe 案例。

speaker: Unknown
en: What founder trait do you refuse to compromise on?
zh: 你拒绝在哪种创始人特质上妥协？

speaker: Unknown
en: Intensity.
zh: 强烈程度。

speaker: Unknown
en: Intensity is important.
zh: 强烈程度很重要。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's too hard to build a big business.
zh: 建立一家 big 大生意太难了。

speaker: Unknown
en: You need intensity.
zh: 你需要强烈程度。

speaker: Unknown
en: Which fund, when you hear are competing, do you go, oh shit, we need to bring out A-game?
zh: 哪个基金，当你听说在竞争时，你会想，噢该死，我们需要拿出 A-game（最佳状态）？

speaker: Unknown
en: I don't think we can be condescending and say we don't bring our A game, no matter who the competitor is.
zh: 我认为我们不能摆出居高临下的态度说我们不拿出我们的 A-game，不管竞争对手是谁。

speaker: Unknown
en: But I know you want names.
zh: 但我知道你想要名字。

speaker: Unknown
en: Can I answer with a story?
zh: 我可以用一个故事来回答吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah.
zh: 可以。

speaker: Unknown
en: So I never lost a deal, an investment in my time at Sequoia, but I've lost investments before.
zh: 所以我从未在一笔交易上失利过，我在红杉期间从未失去过投资，但我以前失去过投资。

speaker: Unknown
en: I lost my first investment two weeks into the job when I started in venture a long time ago.
zh: 我在很久以前刚开始做风投时，入职两周就失去了我的第一笔投资。

speaker: Unknown
en: And that company was revolute, incredible, incredibly painful.
zh: 那家公司是 revolute，incredible 不可思议的，极其 painful 痛苦。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think Index and Bolderton did that round, if I remember correctly.
zh: 我想 Index 和 Bolderton 做了那一轮，如果我记忆正确的话。

speaker: Unknown
en: But basically the story is I'm two weeks into venture.
zh: 但基本上故事是我进入风投两周。

speaker: Unknown
en: Like you, I'm like 20 years old.
zh: 像你一样，我大概 20 岁。

speaker: Unknown
en: I don't know anyone.
zh: 我谁都不认识。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I call up the one person I know in venture capital, Sia from Seedcamp, and he tells me, you should come to that pitch.
zh: 我打给我在风投界认识的唯一一个人，Seedcamp 的 Sia，他告诉我，你应该来那个推介会。

speaker: Unknown
en: We have 10 companies.
zh: 我们有 10 家公司。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I thought, oh, great, 10 companies.
zh: 我想了想，噢，太好了，10 家公司。

speaker: Unknown
en: That's amazing.
zh: 那太棒了。

speaker: Unknown
en: That was the only criteria that I was given.
zh: 那是我得到的唯一标准。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I show up to this rundown place in East London on a basement, and there's 10 founders pitching.
zh: 我出现在东伦敦那个破败地方的地下室，有 10 位创始人在推介。

speaker: Unknown
en: One of them is Nikolai from Revolut.
zh: 其中一位是 Revolut 的 Nikolai。

speaker: Unknown
en: Another one of them is Daniel Dines from UiPath.
zh: 另一位是 UiPath 的 Daniel Dines。

speaker: Unknown
en: Think about the concentration of EV that was just in that day.
zh: 想想那天仅仅存在的 EV（期望值）密度。

speaker: Unknown
en: And they're both raising their seed in Series A. I think Nikolai was the most obvious founder call I've had in my career.
zh: 而且他们都在筹集他们的种子轮和 Series A 轮。我想 Nikolai 是我职业生涯中最明显的创始人选择。

speaker: Unknown
en: It was just so obvious how intense he was.
zh: 他的强烈程度是如此明显。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I proceeded to camp out of his office in Canary Wharf.
zh: 然后我接着去他在 Canary Wharf 的办公室外驻扎。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I just tried to identify him in the crowd every day.
zh: 我每天都试图在人群中认出他。

speaker: Unknown
en: Because he wouldn't respond to my emails, my colleague and I ended up having a meeting with Vlad, his co-founder.
zh: 因为他不回我的邮件，我和我的同事最后见了 Vlad，他的联合创始人。

speaker: Unknown
en: And after trying to convince them to invest, they said that they would go with a competitor.
zh: 在试图说服他们投资之后，他们说他们会选择一家竞争对手。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I was really crushed.
zh: 我真的崩溃了。

speaker: Unknown
en: I remember thinking this could be bigger than PayPal.
zh: 我记得当时在想，这可能比 PayPal 还要大。

speaker: Unknown
en: We'll see.
zh: 我们拭目以待。

speaker: Unknown
en: Time will tell.
zh: 时间会证明一切。

speaker: Unknown
en: But it's, I think, a fantastic business.
zh: 但我认为，这是一家很棒的公司。

speaker: Unknown
en: But at that time, I tried my chances and I said, can I invest personally in the company?
zh: 但在那个时候，我碰碰运气，并问道，我可以个人投资这家公司吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: And they begrudgingly pointed me to an SPV, but I was penniless at the time.
zh: 他们不情愿地把我指向了一个 SPV，但我当时身无分文。

speaker: Unknown
en: And even though I had the opportunity, I didn't know how to fund the commitment.
zh: 尽管我有这个机会，但我不知道如何筹集这笔承诺的资金。

speaker: Unknown
en: So I remember calling my mom on the way back.
zh: 所以我记得在回来的路上给我妈妈打了电话。

speaker: Unknown
en: Like your mom, she's always been there for me for business decisions.
zh: 就像你妈妈一样，她一直在商业决策上支持我。

speaker: Unknown
en: And she said, that sounds like a pretty good idea.
zh: 她说，这听起来是个很不错的主意。

speaker: Unknown
en: How about I give you the money, but we'll do 50-50?
zh: 我给你这笔钱怎么样，但我们五五分？

speaker: Unknown
en: 10 years later, I've only kept buying shares in the business.
zh: 10 年后，我一直在购买这家公司的股份。

speaker: Unknown
en: I haven't sold one, but my mom just sold most of her shares and she just retired at 74 years old.
zh: 我没有卖过一股，但我妈妈刚刚卖掉了她的大部分股份，她刚在 74 岁退休了。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so I always joke with my partners that they could only hire the second best investor in the Beck family because my mom went all in on Revolut at the Series A.
zh: 所以我总是跟我的合作伙伴开玩笑说，他们只能雇佣 Beck 家族第二好的投资者，因为我妈妈在 A 轮（Series A）全仓押注了 Revolut。

speaker: Unknown
en: What multiple is that?
zh: 那是几倍的回报？

speaker: Unknown
en: I'm not asking for money, but just like... Well, it depends on what valuation, but we entered at $200, no, $180, $200 million.
zh: 我不是在要钱，只是像……嗯，这取决于估值，但我们是在 2 亿，不，1.8 亿，2 亿美元时进入的。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think the latest valuation is over $100 billion.
zh: 我认为最新的估值超过 1000 亿美元。

speaker: Unknown
en: Just tell your mom to have one line on her track record.
zh: 只要告诉你妈妈在她的战绩上留下一笔就行。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah, exactly.
zh: 是的，完全正确。

speaker: Unknown
en: Revlon, Pat, Mic Drop.
zh: Revlon，Pat，Mic Drop。

speaker: Unknown
en: Exactly, exactly.
zh: 没错，没错。

speaker: Unknown
en: Well done, mom.
zh: 干得好，妈妈。

speaker: Unknown
en: You know what?
zh: 你知道吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: It's not about who finds it, it's about who gets the cash at the end of the day.
zh: 这不在于谁发现了它，而在于谁最终拿到了现金。

speaker: Unknown
en: That's unbelievable.
zh: 真是难以置信。

speaker: Unknown
en: Do you know what though?
zh: 但你知道吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: This is why I'll be forever unhappy.
zh: 这就是为什么我会永远不开心。

speaker: Unknown
en: You know what I always think in those situations?
zh: 你知道我在那种情况下总是怎么想的吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: If only I put double my checks.
zh: 要是我把支票金额加倍就好了。

speaker: Unknown
en: That's amazing, I love that.
zh: 太神奇了，我喜欢这一点。

speaker: Unknown
en: Well, I earned 30K at the time, so it was really bad.
zh: 嗯，我当时赚 3 万，所以真的很糟糕。

speaker: Unknown
en: Actually, at the time, I worked for this guy, Olly Samwer, who was the founder of Rocket Internet.
zh: 实际上，在那个时候，我为这个人工作，Olly Samwer，Rocket Internet 的创始人。

speaker: Unknown
en: And he's amazing for so many things, but everyone knows he's a very tough negotiator.
zh: 他很多事情都很了不起，但大家都知道他是一个非常强硬的谈判者。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so when I joined his company, I said that I wanted more than 30K, and he refused.
zh: 所以当我加入他的公司时，我说我想要超过 3 万，但他拒绝了。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so I actually was able to negotiate that I was going to be able to invest in the companies in order to make enough money to survive from the investments.
zh: 所以实际上我能够谈判达成，我将能够投资这些公司，以便从投资中赚取足够的钱来生存。

speaker: Unknown
en: And actually, you know, those angel checks are, you know, pretty, pretty healthy these days.
zh: 实际上，你知道，那些天使支票现在非常，非常健康。

speaker: Unknown
en: Preseed and Atio, Albert, Revolut.
zh: Preseed 和 Atio，Albert，Revolut。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah, but my mom still has the best track record.
zh: 是的，但我妈妈仍然拥有最好的战绩。

speaker: Unknown
en: She missed all the bad ones.
zh: 她避开了所有那些糟糕的。

speaker: Unknown
en: That is fantastic.
zh: 这太棒了。

speaker: Unknown
en: What do you believe about venture capital that most of the Sequoia partnership would disagree with?
zh: 关于风险投资，你相信什么，而 Sequoia 的大多数合伙人会不同意？

speaker: Unknown
en: Oh, the funny thing is people love to say Sequoia believes X and Y, but we actually have very different opinions.
zh: 哦，有趣的是人们喜欢说 Sequoia 相信 X 和 Y，但实际上我们意见非常不同。

speaker: Unknown
en: There's no house view on AI.
zh: 对 AI 没有统一的内部观点。

speaker: Unknown
en: I can post this article about services being the new software while simultaneously you'll have David Kahn talking about the $600 billion question and simultaneously Pat and Sonia saying this is AGI.
zh: 我可以发布这篇关于服务是新软件的文章，同时你会看到 David Kahn 在谈论 6000 亿美元的问题，同时 Pat 和 Sonia 说这是 AGI。

speaker: Unknown
en: Make it hard then because I'd be annoyed if I believe in the services element and then another one of my partners puts out a piece saying something very different and opposing.
zh: 那这就很难了，因为如果我坚信服务的要素，然后我的另一个合伙人发表一篇言论非常不同且相反的文章，我会很恼火。

speaker: Unknown
en: I'd worry that the founders that I'm trying to attract with mine are reading theirs going, well, we're not going to go to them.
zh: 我会担心我试图吸引的创始人读了他们的文章后想，好吧，我们不会去找他们。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah, but at the same time, you know, you cannot be bland.
zh: 是的，但同时，你知道，你不能平淡无奇。

speaker: Unknown
en: You want people to seek you out for who you are.
zh: 你希望人们因为你是谁而主动找上门。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's what people forget about a brand, which is like the best brands make you feel something.
zh: 这是人们关于品牌容易忘记的一点，就像最好的品牌会让你产生某种感觉。

speaker: Unknown
en: Exactly.
zh: 没错。

speaker: Unknown
en: The worst is meh.
zh: 最糟糕的就是平淡乏味。

speaker: Unknown
en: For or against Nike or Adidas, Apple or Windows, you feel something?
zh: 不管是支持还是反对耐克或阿迪达斯，苹果或 Windows，你会有感觉吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: We're trying to invest in spiky people, so we have to be spiky ourselves.
zh: 我们正试图投资那些有棱角的人，所以我们自己必须也得有棱角。

speaker: Unknown
en: Final one.
zh: 最后一个问题。

speaker: Unknown
en: What are you most excited for about the next five years of AI, about what will change, what will happen?
zh: 关于未来五年的 AI，关于会有什么改变，会发生什么，你最兴奋的是什么？

speaker: Unknown
en: Again, I think it's what I told you before.
zh: 同样，我想这就是我之前告诉过你的。

speaker: Unknown
en: We're still in this phase where AI is maybe 120 IQ with the latest tests, but when we get to 500 IQ AIs, we'll maybe find cures for your mom or my dad's disease.
